classification.difficultyReason: Apply the sine rule and its supplementary-angle relationship to two supplied triangles.

content.prompt: Two triangles are shown, with sides 6 cm and 4 cm. The angle opposite the 4 cm side is $36^{\circ}$. Find, in each case, the angle opposite the 6 cm side, correct to the nearest degree.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2: horizontal pair of supplied triangles beneath the prompt, towards the right.
spec.description: Two unshaded triangles with horizontal bases. The left triangle has an obtuse left-base angle and its upper vertex lies left of that base vertex. The right triangle has an acute left-base angle. Both right-base angles are labelled 36°, with opposite sides labelled 4 cm and upper-to-right sides labelled 6 cm.
spec.mathematics: For each figure, the upper vertex is 6 units from the right-base vertex along a ray at 144°. The left-base vertices are the two intersections of the horizontal baseline with a circle of radius 4 centred at the upper vertex.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied lengths and 36° angles are visible; the requested angles are absent.

answer.short: Left triangle: $118^{\circ}$; right triangle: $62^{\circ}$. The two angles are supplementary.
answer.worked:
Let $\alpha$ be the acute angle opposite the 6 cm side.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{\sin\alpha}{6}&=\frac{\sin36^{\circ}}{4}\\\sin\alpha&=\frac{6\sin36^{\circ}}{4}\\\alpha&=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{6\sin36^{\circ}}{4}\right)\\\alpha&\approx62^{\circ}.\end{aligned}$$
Using the unrounded value of $\alpha$, the other possible angle is
$$\begin{aligned}\beta&=180^{\circ}-\alpha\\\beta&\approx118^{\circ}.\end{aligned}$$
Both possibilities are valid: $\alpha+36^{\circ}<180^{\circ}$ and $\beta+36^{\circ}<180^{\circ}$. Therefore the left triangle has angle $118^{\circ}$ and the right triangle has angle $62^{\circ}$, to the nearest degree.
